subject: MAP & perf validation: chat TTFT + streaming latency plan and initial results
messages:
From: Simon Lee <simon.lee@acuitymed.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 08:03:22 -0500
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff & perf ask — baseline expectations

Priyom / team,

Thanks for the kickoff call this morning — attaching our MAP draft (AcuityMed-MAP-draft.xlsx) with milestones and the timelines we discussed. To make the evaluation concrete, here are the perf targets we care about for chat generation in production:

- Expected peak concurrent users (chat sessions): 150 active sessions, with spikes to 400 for short windows.
- Typical prompt length: 80 tokens; response target length: 220 tokens average.
- Hard SLO for Time-to-First-Token (TTFT): p95 <= 350ms, p99 <= 600ms.
- Streaming latency (per-token to client): p95 <= 60ms.
- Sustained throughput target: ~30k tokens/sec for steady-state customer traffic.

We'd like Redwood to run a benchmark that measures TTFT (p50/p95/p99), streaming per-token latencies (p50/p95/p99), and throughput at the concurrency points: 1, 8, 32, 128, 400. Also please include token-length sensitivity (short / medium / long responses).

Can you confirm the proposed test plan and give an expected date for results? We need these numbers to finalize the MAP close timeline by end of the month.

—Simon
Simon Lee
Lead Customer Engineer, AcuityMed

---

On Fri, Feb 20, 2026 at 10:15 AM Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com> wrote:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Simon Lee <simon.lee@acuitymed.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 10:15:41 -0500
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff & perf ask — baseline expectations

Simon — thanks for the clear targets and the MAP draft. We can run an evaluation that matches those concurrency breakpoints and report TTFT + streaming and throughput across three response length buckets (short: 40-80 tokens, medium: 180-260, long: 400+).

High-level plan (attached: rw_benchmark_plan_20260220.pdf):
- Controlled bench in Redwood Dedicated test pool (A100 80GB, 1x model replica per GPU) using rw-3b-q4 quantized variant and a streaming-enabled runtime.
- Warm cache runs (1000 requests) then steady-state ramps for each concurrency point.
- Metrics: TTFT (time from request acceptance to first token emitted), per-token streaming latency, tokens/sec, and end-to-end response tail.
- We'll capture p50/p95/p99 for each metric and upload raw traces/logs + aggregate CSV.

Proposed timeline:
- Monday (Feb 22): Redwood runs bench and shares raw CSV + initial summary.
- Tues (Feb 23): Q&A and follow-up runs for any corner cases.
- Wed (Feb 24): Final MAP update and consolidated results for your procurement team.

If you want higher-fidelity results on your exact VPC setup we can also run a private deployment replicate, but that will add ~1 week. For MAP close, the Dedicated pool numbers should be sufficient to validate perf economics.

I'll loop in Ben and Dev for the run and logs.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Simon Lee <simon.lee@acuitymed.com>, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 22 Feb 2026 16:40:12 -0500
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff & perf ask — preliminary benchmark results (raw)

Attaching: benchmark-run-20260221.csv (summary) and run-logs-20260221.tar.gz (traces). High-level callouts below — ran on rw-3b-q4, A100 80GB dedicated pool, 1 replica per GPU, streaming enabled, kernel optimizations on.

Summary tables (selected):
- Concurrency = 1 (single session) — avg response ~220 tokens
  - TTFT p50 = 82 ms
  - TTFT p95 = 210 ms
  - TTFT p99 = 380 ms
  - Streaming per-token latency p50 = 9 ms, p95 = 24 ms, p99 = 72 ms
  - Throughput (tokens/sec sustained) = 320 tps
- Concurrency = 8 (small burst)
  - TTFT p50 = 95 ms
  - TTFT p95 = 260 ms
  - TTFT p99 = 430 ms
  - Streaming per-token latency p50 = 12 ms, p95 = 34 ms, p99 = 95 ms
  - Throughput (tokens/sec sustained) = 2,100 tps (aggregate across replicas)
- Concurrency = 32
  - TTFT p50 = 150 ms
  - TTFT p95 = 420 ms
  - TTFT p99 = 720 ms
  - Streaming per-token latency p50 = 20 ms, p95 = 58 ms, p99 = 150 ms
  - Throughput (tokens/sec sustained) = 6,800 tps
- Concurrency = 128
  - TTFT p50 = 510 ms
  - TTFT p95 = 940 ms
  - TTFT p99 = 1,480 ms
  - Streaming per-token latency p50 = 55 ms, p95 = 120 ms, p99 = 280 ms
  - Throughput (tokens/sec sustained) = 18,500 tps
- Concurrency = 400 (stress)
  - TTFT p50 = 1,420 ms
  - TTFT p95 = 2,600 ms
  - TTFT p99 = 4,100 ms
  - Streaming per-token latency p50 = 190 ms, p95 = 420 ms, p99 = 1,100 ms
  - Throughput (tokens/sec sustained) = 28,900 tps (note: increased variance and tail latencies; observed occasional queueing/backpressure)

Notes / interpretation:
- At your stated steady-state target (~30k tps) we approach the upper bounds of a single dedicated pool config; multiple replicas or larger pool sizing will provide headroom and reduce tail.
- TTFT SLOs (p95 <= 350ms, p99 <= 600ms): we meet p95 at lower concurrencies (<=8) and p99 at <=8, but p99 breaches at 32+ for the current config.
- Streaming p95 <= 60ms: met up to concurrency 32; at 128 and 400 p95 exceeds target.
- We captured kernel-level traces and queue length metrics in the attached CSV for you to inspect.

Next steps: if Acuity wants to validate an optimized setup we can test: (a) increased replica count, (b) quantization profile changes, and (c) prefix cache priming. I recommend a follow-up run focused on 32–128 concurrencies with 2x replicas to measure tail improvement.

—Ben
Ben Carter
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff & perf ask — preliminary benchmark results (raw)

Thanks Ben — great detail and appreciated. A few quick follow-ups:

1) Can you upload the raw per-request logs (latency by request id) and the exact request payloads used for each length bucket? We want to run the same harness on our end.
2) For the 128/400 concurrency runs — were those single replica tests (queued) or multi-replica? If single replica, I'd like to see the 2x replica run you suggested.
3) If we need to meet p99 <= 600ms at 128 concurrency, what's the recommended Dedicated configuration (replica count / GPU type / cache strategy)? Estimate of monthly cost delta would be helpful for the MAP.

If we can get an updated run by Wed with the 2x replica for 32–128 and the raw CSVs, we'll aim to finalize procurement for the Dedicated pool.

—Simon

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Simon Lee <simon.lee@acuitymed.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 14:22:05 -0500
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff & perf ask — updated MAP and next steps

Simon — attaching the updated MAP (MAP-final-20260224.xlsx) and the run artifacts (run-logs-20260221.tar.gz). Quick answers and plan: 

- Raw logs & harness: attached in run-logs-20260221.tar.gz and uploaded to the Drive link above. The CSV includes per-request ids, timestamps, and kernel-level timing buckets.
- 128/400 runs were single-replica stress tests to show system behaviour at saturation; the 2x replica runs (32 & 128 targets) complete this morning — results are in the Drive and summarized below.

2x-replica summary (rw-3b-q4, 2 replicas, A100 80GB each, streaming enabled):
- Concurrency = 32 (2 replicas)
  - TTFT p50 = 92 ms, p95 = 210 ms, p99 = 340 ms
  - Streaming per-token p95 = 34 ms, p99 = 82 ms
  - Throughput = 7,200 tps (aggregate)

- Concurrency = 128 (2 replicas)
  - TTFT p50 = 240 ms, p95 = 490 ms, p99 = 720 ms
  - Streaming per-token p95 = 75 ms, p99 = 190 ms
  - Throughput = 19,800 tps

Interpretation and MAP impacts:
- With 2x replicas we bring p95 TTFT below your 350ms SLO at 128 concurrency, but p99 at 128 still sits above the strict 600ms threshold. If p99 at 128 is a firm requirement, recommended options: add a third replica or provision a higher-throughput GPU profile (DGX-style pooling) for the sustained peak windows.
- Cost delta estimate (very rough): +35% to Dedicated monthly commit for 3 replicas vs 2 replicas (depends on burst policy and reserved vs on-demand). We'll include a precise pricing line in the MAP workbook.

Proposed MAP close timeline (updated):
- Wed Feb 25: Acuity procurement reviews MAP-final; Redwood to provide final pricing addendum.
- Fri Feb 27: Contract redline exchange.
- Mon Mar 2: Target Dedicated provision and onboarding window (can accelerate if procurement signs earlier).

Action items:
- (Redwood) Provide final pricing addendum and 3-replica estimate by EOD Wed.
- (Acuity) Confirm whether p99 <= 600ms at 128 must be a hard SLO or a best-effort target.
- (Both) Schedule a 30m follow-up to review run-level CSVs if needed.

Marissa will own the MAP pricing sheet; Ben/Dev will own the bench-run artifacts. I'll shepherd the contract workflow.

Thanks — will follow up with the pricing addendum shortly.

Best,
Priyom Das
